title: Red Light, Green Light Dribble
description: A classic stop-and-go game for young players: dribble forward on green, jump-stop on red, and keep the ball alive the whole time.

content.objective: Start, stop and change speed while keeping control of the dribble, finishing each stop with a balanced jump stop.
content.setup: Players line up on the baseline with a ball each. The coach stands at the half-court line facing them.
content.organization: Whole group races together. First to tag the coach becomes the next caller.
instructions: On 'green light', players dribble forward toward the coach.
On 'yellow light', they slow to a walk while keeping the dribble going.
On 'red light', they jump-stop with both feet and catch the ball in triple threat.
Anyone who travels, double-dribbles or loses the ball returns to the baseline.
The first player to reach and tag the coach wins the round and calls the next one.
coachingPoints: Stop on two feet at the same time.
Catch the ball and hold it at the hip on red.
Keep the eyes on the coach to react first.
commonMistakes: Sliding a foot after the stop (travel).
Restarting the dribble after catching on red (double dribble).
Watching the ball and missing the call.
content.safety: Run lanes must be wide enough that players are never shoulder to shoulder; stop the game if anyone dives for a ball.
progressions: Require the weak hand on green.
Add 'turn' (pivot 180 degrees) as an extra light.
regressions: Allow a two-hand pick-up instead of a jump stop.
Shorten the distance to the free-throw line.
variations: Players are the caller in pairs.
Use a whistle code instead of words.
successCriteria: Reaches the coach without a violation.
Every red-light stop is a two-foot stop with the ball protected.
content.gameApplication: Stopping under control is how young players avoid travels at the end of drives and on the catch.
